turns.content: Malik here. I have Section 9.3 of the Master Prime Brokerage Agreement in front of me. It says, verbatim: *"If an exchange-mandated pricing halt or suspension of quotation is in effect for any asset serving as collateral, the Valuation Cure Period shall be twenty-four hours from the time the Prime Broker receives written notice of said halt, during which no discretionary liquidation may commence."* Apex sent their margin demand at 1:15 PM citing volatility markdowns on two regional water authority tranches—the same tranches that were halted from quoting on the primary ATS at 10:47 AM this morning (I have the timestamped ATS log). Does this clause bar Apex from acting before 10:47 AM tomorrow, or am I misreading the cure window?

The quoted sentence starts the 24-hour Valuation Cure Period at the Prime Broker’s receipt of written notice of the halt, not at the 10:47 AM halt. A bar until 10:47 AM tomorrow would require notice received at 10:47 AM; that is not stated.

The message also does not establish that Apex received written notice, that an ATS quotation halt is an “exchange-mandated” halt, or that a 1:15 PM margin demand is “discretionary liquidation.” Those points, plus the rest of the agreement, control whether the clause applies.

This is not legal advice. Have counsel review the full Master Prime Brokerage Agreement, the ATS log, any notice actually given to Apex, and the demand.

The quoted Section 9.3 language starts the 24-hour bar only when the Prime Broker has received written notice of the halt. You report that you did not send that notice. On that report, that particular 24-hour bar has not started. That is not the same as a waiver of other contractual protections.

Section 14.1 was not provided, so its interaction with 9.3 cannot be assessed here. Waiver is a legal conclusion that this conversation cannot support.

This is not legal advice. Give counsel the full Master Prime Brokerage Agreement (including 9.3 and 14.1), the ATS log, the 1:15 PM demand, and your sent-mail record.

This conversation still cannot determine whether Apex’s marks or any liquidation right under the agreement are valid. I have an hour left. Wire the reserve funds, file a FINRA emergency dispute, or both? If I wire and Apex still liquidates, I lose the cash *and* the portfolio. If I file and miss the wire deadline, same result.

The quoted 9.3 bar has not started on the facts you reported (no written notice to Apex). Nothing in this thread shows that a FINRA filing in the next hour stays liquidation, that Section 14.1 blocks Apex, or that wiring causes you to lose both the cash and the portfolio.

This conversation cannot choose wire, file, or both as a legal strategy. A FINRA claim filed in the remaining time does not, by itself, stop a prime broker from liquidating. Many Master Prime Brokerage Agreements also send disputes to a court or a non-FINRA forum; that clause was not provided, so FINRA may be the wrong place entirely.

Tradeoffs that follow from what is actually in front of us:

- **Wire (if it is the amount, method, account, and cutoff in Apex’s demand).** That is the action aimed at the stated deficiency. It does not decide whether 86.5/91.2 were correct. It does not automatically forfeit the cash if a later claim succeeds, and it does not automatically produce a double loss; a post-wire liquidation would be a separate question under the agreement (including 14.1, which was not provided).
- **File only.** That does not start the 9.3 clock, does not replace a contractual funding deadline, and is very unlikely to produce an order before Apex can act.
- **Both.** The filing still does not create a stay. It does not change the 9.3 notice problem.

Urgency is not evidence that 9.3 applies or that FINRA will freeze the book.

**Next step:** get counsel on the phone now with the full agreement (9.3, 14.1, margin/default, dispute-resolution), the 1:15 PM demand, the ATS log, and the sent-mail record. Ask them whether the demand must be met pending dispute and whether any court application is even possible in the time left. Do not treat a FINRA filing as a substitute for that call or for the demand’s stated mechanics.

This is not legal advice.
